comment: Dear Chris, Myself and several of my neighbors were recently contacted by the city about our rock landscaped park strips. According to city code they are not in compliance with the 33% vegetation requirement. My yard has been landscaped this way for years and I feel that enforcing this code during a mega drought is extremely irresponsible. I do have a well cared for Ginko tree on my park strip that once full grown will provide a multitude of benefits. I do not feel comfortable planting and watering more plants in the current climate. I would rather like to focus on conserving water and keeping alive the plants that are established. I agree that waterwise vegetation is a nice idea, however it is hard to maintain and it still requires water. I would hope that as our representative you can bring this to the attention of the mayoral office. The city should be providing grants for water wise plants on park strips and encouraging water saving measures rather than trying to enforce a code I find more detrimental than good. Thank you for your time, -- Rachel Simeon

This message is from Sissy Tan, a D3 constituent, calling to discuss City ordinance that requires 1/3 of the front property to be landscaped and maintained. She does not think the ordinance is appropriate during these current times and to enforce it while we are in a drought is unwise. Ms. Tan wonders if you would be willing to help suspend the enforcement of this ordinance.

Chris, This message is from Sue Royzer calling to express how happy she is that SLCPD will increase enforcement of the noise ordinance. She says she recently heard about this in the local news (https://www.ksl.com/article/50219294/ksl-investigates-unbearable-street-noise-lack-of-enforcement) and says it's the best news she's received since moving to Salt Lake City.
